question.text: Will the Belgian State and Engie conclude an agreement for Belgium's acquisition of Engie's nuclear activities before December 14, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as **Yes** if, before December 14, 2026 (Central European Time), according to [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) the Belgian State and Engie S.A. and/or Electrabel formally agree to a Heads of Terms (HoT) for the Belgian State's acquisition of Engie's Belgian nuclear activities. The question resolves as **No** if no qualifying agreement has been concluded by the deadline. An extension alone does not count as a qualifying agreement.
question.fine_print: An agreement counts even if it covers only part of the assets originally under discussion. An agreement may be variously described as Heads of Terms, a protocol of agreement, or a memorandum of understanding. An "agreement in principle" that has not been formalised, an approval by only one side, or statements that a deal is close or imminent do not count.

research:
I'm writing up the findings now. No Heads of Terms had been signed as of 20 November 2026. The current target date is 12 December, two days before the question deadline.

## 1. Resolution source
- No single data series decides this question. It turns on credible reports of a formal Heads of Terms (HoT) or memorandum of understanding (MoU). The likely primary source is the Engie newsroom, which announced each earlier step.
- 2026-11-04: The latest official status. The Belgian State, ENGIE S.A. and Electrabel moved the HoT target date to **12 December 2026**, calling it "a maximum extension of one additional month." They said talks had progressed but "significant differences remain, notably regarding the valuation of the transaction." [Engie newsroom](https://en.newsroom.engie.com/news/the-belgian-state-and-engie-group-have-agreed-to-extend-the-target-date-for-concluding-the-heads-of-terms-until-12-december-2026-7ced5-314df.html); [Euronext](https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/engie-and-belgium-government-take-more-time-conclude-deal-over-engies-nuclear-assets)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. I found no report of a signed HoT up to 20 November.
- Under the criteria, a fourth extension would count as No.
- 12 December 2026 is a Saturday, so a signing or announcement on 11 to 13 December would still fall inside the window.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-19: De Standaard reports that Electrabel CEO Cedric Osterrieth told staff that without a framework agreement by 12 December, dismantling of the closed reactors will resume. I could not fetch this page myself; the summary comes from the news feed and La Libre. [De Standaard](https://www.standaard.be/economie/zonder-akkoord-wil-engie-vanaf-12-december-kernreactoren-verder-ontmantelen/164781839.html)
- 2026-11-18/19: La Libre calls this an Engie "ultimatum": management describes 12 December as final, and without a deal Engie would go back to its pre-29 April position. Two sticking points:
  - **Dismantling money:** the state wants Engie to pay a top-up for under-funded dismantling provisions, and the gap is "several billion euros."
  - **Scope:** Engie wants the state to take all of Tractebel, its engineering firm, while the government wants only the nuclear branch.
  - Some observers think Engie is bluffing. Staff fear that if the government collapses, the deal dies with it. The energy minister's office declined to comment. [La Libre](https://www.lalibre.be/economie/conjoncture/2026/11/18/engie-lance-un-ultimatum-un-accord-sur-la-nationalisation-du-parc-nucleaire-doit-etre-trouve-dici-decembre-QZ3EAVZ5EZD2NHGUE642VPQ62I/)
- 2026-11-04: Second postponement. Energy Minister Bihet has said the 7% return Engie got under earlier deals is too high. [VRT](https://www.vrt.be/vrtnws/nl/2026/11/04/akkoord-over-overname-van-kerncentrales-alweer-uitgesteld/); [PAL](https://pal.be/2026/11/regering-en-engie-raken-het-niet-eens-over-de-kerncentrales/)
- 2026-09-30: First postponement, from 1 October to 4 November, citing "complexity and scale." [Refrance](https://refrance.fr/nucleaire-belge-engie-et-letat-repoussent-au-4-novembre-leur-protocole-daccord/)
- 2026-04-29/30: Non-binding letter of intent and exclusive talks covering all seven reactors, staff, subsidiaries and liabilities. Dismantling was suspended during the talks. [Engie newsroom](https://newsroom.engie.com/actualites/l-etat-belge-et-le-groupe-engie-entament-des-negociations-exclusives-pour-l-acquisition-des-activites-nucleaires-d-engie-par-la-belgique-54e28-ff316.html); [VRT](https://www.vrt.be/vrtnws/nl/2026/04/30/engie-federale-regering-nucleaire-activiteiten/)

## 4. Base rates
- In this negotiation, 0 of 2 target dates have been met (1 October and 4 November). Both were missed and extended.
- The closest precedent is the 2022-2023 Engie and Belgian State deal on extending Doel 4 and Tihange 3:
  - 2022-07-22: agreement in principle.
  - 2023-06-28/29: interim agreement.
  - 2023-12-13: final agreement signed.
  - In total about 19 months, with several slipped deadlines, but each stage was eventually formalised. [VRT 2022](https://www.vrt.be/vrtnws/nl/2022/07/22/regering-en-engie-nemen-eerste-horde-in-onderhandelingen-over-ve/); [VRT 2023](https://www.vrt.be/vrtnws/nl/2023/12/13/engie-deal-ondertekening/); [La Libre](https://www.lalibre.be/economie/conjoncture/2023/12/13/le-gouvernement-et-engie-ont-signe-laccord-sur-le-nucleaire-pendant-trop-longtemps-il-ny-a-pas-eu-de-politique-energetique-dans-ce-pays-IKFGOK5JMVEAROJ6GNLMGFOKPQ/)
- Separately, there is still a dispute of more than €2 billion between the state and Engie over nuclear provisions. [search summary of La Libre coverage](https://www.lalibre.be/economie/conjoncture/2026/11/18/engie-lance-un-ultimatum-un-accord-sur-la-nationalisation-du-parc-nucleaire-doit-etre-trouve-dici-decembre-QZ3EAVZ5EZD2NHGUE642VPQ62I/)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- **By 12 December 2026:** the HoT target date. Three outcomes are possible:
  - signed HoT, which resolves Yes;
  - another extension, which resolves No despite Engie calling 12 December final;
  - talks collapse and dismantling resumes.
- **Federal coalition stability:** I found no sign of a budget crisis in November 2026, but my search was limited. A government collapse would likely derail the talks.
- **Things to watch:** Engie newsroom releases, statements from De Wever or Bihet's offices, and La Libre, De Standaard, L'Echo and De Tijd reporting in early December. Note that the photo caption in La Libre's article says De Wever is weighing forced nationalisation, which would not count as an agreement.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 3 weeks remain, with the target date on 12 December 2026 and the question deadline on 14 December CET. For Yes, the Belgian State and Engie/Electrabel must formally sign and announce a Heads of Terms, protocol or MoU for the state's acquisition of the nuclear activities, even a partial one, by 13 December. Another extension or an unformalised "agreement in principle" resolves No.

(b) The status quo is No. There is no signed HoT, "significant differences remain" on valuation, and the default outcomes are another extension or a breakdown.

(c) Base rate:
- In this negotiation, 0 of 2 target dates have produced a HoT, and both ended in last-minute extensions.
- Large state-corporate energy deals with "final" deadlines are typically signed at or near the final deadline maybe 35-45% of the time. They are frequently extended again.
- The Doel 4/Tihange 3 precedent shows Engie and the Belgian State do eventually formalise agreements, but with repeated slippage.
- Starting base rate: about 35%.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- The 4 November extension was explicitly labelled a "maximum" one-month extension.
- Engie's ultimatum, reported 18-19 November in La Libre and De Standaard, raises pressure to close by 12 December.
- Both sides have strong incentives. Engie wants out of nuclear exposure, and the government wants to keep the reactors and stop dismantling.
- On 5 November, MacGregor expressed confidence in good-faith talks.

Evidence for No:
- The gap on decommissioning top-ups is reported at several billion euros, and the Tractebel scope dispute is unresolved (18 November).
- The federal government is in crisis. De Wever offered his resignation on 2 November, and his budget mission was extended to 23 November. A caretaker or collapsing government would struggle to sign a multi-billion acquisition.
- Some observers think Engie is bluffing, which implies a further extension is plausible.
- De Wever is reportedly weighing forced nationalisation, which would not count.

(e) No scenario: budget talks stay stuck or the government falls. On 11-12 December the parties announce a further short extension "to finalise," or talks break off and Engie announces it is resuming dismantling.

Yes scenario: the budget crisis is patched in late November. With Engie's dismantling threat looming, the parties split the decommissioning gap and narrow the Tractebel scope. A HoT is signed and announced by press release on 11-12 December.

(f) I start at 35%. The "maximum" wording and the ultimatum push up slightly, but the government instability and the multi-billion valuation gap with three weeks left push down. Overall I land just below the base rate, at about 32%.

Probability: 32%

(a) Time left and what Yes requires: About 3.5 weeks remain, with the outcome known by 14 December 2026. Yes requires that, before that date, the Belgian State and Engie and/or Electrabel formally sign a Heads of Terms, protocol or MoU for the state's acquisition of the nuclear activities. The current target date is 12 December. Another extension or a statement that a deal is "close" counts as No.

(b) Status quo: No agreement. Talks have missed two deadlines and serious differences remain, so the status quo outcome is No.

(c) Base rate: Within this negotiation, 0 of 2 target dates have produced an agreement. Large state-corporate deals facing a "final" deadline with a multi-billion valuation gap close on that deadline perhaps 30-40% of the time. Otherwise they slip or collapse. The 2022-2023 Engie and Belgian State deal on Doel 4 and Tihange 3 was eventually formalised, but only after repeated slippage. Base rate: about 35%.

(d) Strongest evidence:
- For Yes:
  - 2026-11-04: The extension was labelled "a maximum," which creates pressure to finish.
  - 2026-11-18/19: Engie issued an ultimatum that dismantling resumes after 12 December, which forces a decision.
  - 2026-11-05: Engie CEO MacGregor said she expects the government to negotiate in good faith.
  - Both sides have strategic reasons to want the deal, and Belgian deals tend to close at the last minute.
- For No:
  - 2026-11-04: "Significant differences remain, notably regarding valuation."
  - The decommissioning top-up gap is "several billion euros," and the parties also disagree over Tractebel's scope.
  - 2026-11-02: De Wever offered the government's resignation over the budget. The King refused it on 6 November, and the budget crisis is unresolved, with his mission extended to 23 November.
  - A government in crisis is poorly placed to commit billions.
  - A third extension would still resolve No.

(e) Scenarios:
- No: The budget crisis absorbs the government. The valuation gap is not closed by 12 December. Either Engie and the state agree a short "technical" extension, or talks collapse and dismantling resumes. A forced-nationalisation threat would not count as an agreement either.
- Yes: The coalition patches together a budget in late November. Over the weekend of 11-13 December, the parties sign a HoT that leaves the provisions top-up to be finalised later, or that covers a narrower scope such as Tractebel's nuclear branch only. Engie announces it on its newsroom.

(f) Adjustment: I start from about 35%. The ultimatum dynamic and the "maximum" wording push up slightly. The deep valuation gap, two sticking points and a federal government in budget crisis push down more. The likelihood that any slip resolves No also counts against Yes. Net, I land a little below the base rate, at around 30%.

Probability: 30%
